cross_market_insights: No market has a strong, authoritative answer. Top 3 slots are filled by forums (Reddit, Quora, WeddingWire), marketplaces (Easy Weddings, The Knot) and pages with no snippet. The SERP is winnable on quality.
Every figure that ranks is budget tier (roughly 10K to 45K in USD or AUD). Nobody covers the luxury band (AUD 150K+) our couple plans in.

Melbourne and Brisbane SERPs are dominated by HOME wedding cost pages (Q Report, Seasons5, Wedding VIC, Managing Matrimony). Google reads this query in Australia as 'how does it compare with an Australian wedding'. This validates the user's edge: compare destination costs with the Australian home average.
Only one ranking page (RamaRossi, London) frames home vs abroad, and it is UK-focused. No ranking page does it for Australians.

Australian home averages that rank (35,315; 38,252; 36,000 to 54,000) are mostly derived from the Easy Weddings survey, which is a blocked source. An independent benchmark (e.g. ASIC Moneysmart, cited by Swoosh) is the gap.
No ranking page organises costs by region the way an Australian shortlists (Europe, Asia and the Pacific, Middle East). Related searches ask for 'europe', 'australia' and 'per person' variants.
PAA across AU markets: 'Who pays for travel for a destination wedding?' and 'Is it cheaper to do a destination wedding?' recur. Both belong in the FAQ.
Invisible costs (room blocks, currency and deposits across borders, legal paperwork, wet-weather backup, transfers) are absent from every snippet.
Our own Trending page on cost-saving ideas ranks 6 in London on a budget angle; it attracts the anti-persona and should not be linked from this piece.
payload.recommended_angle: A sourced, region-by-region view of what destination weddings cost, set against an independent Australian home-wedding benchmark, written for couples planning in the luxury band. Short regional sections hand off to our existing cost guides, and one section shows the costs no average includes and what an advisor handles.
